title: Intro to Geometry Nodes — transformations and CSG
note: Begin with Cube and Group Output. Change one transformation at a time, compare all three Booleans, then develop a massing study.

title: Geometry Fundamentals
note: The existing lesson is preserved. Point → Line → Edge → Face → Solid → Boolean; pyramid Width, Depth and Height remain exposed.

title: Arrays and Lists I — linear and nested grid
note: Use Repeat Zones with small counts, then repeat a row inside a second loop to make a grid.

title: Arrays and Lists II — arrangements and rules
note: Stagger rows, place points around a circle, select an index range and control a curve with sine.

title: Attractors
note: Read a distance field, remap it, and compare one point, multiple points and a curve.

title: Tessellation and Lattices
note: Compare cells covering a surface with a spatial network. Lattice struts overlap at joints; resolve connections before fabrication.

title: Point Clouds and Volumes
note: Keep teaching-courtyard.ply beside the Blender file. The bundled synthetic dataset includes source, units and license information.

title: Advanced Volumes I — signed distance and Boolean
note: Compare a mesh, a sampled signed distance grid, an analytic sphere field and a volumetric difference.

title: Advanced Volumes II — noise and surface extraction
note: Control a scalar field with noise and extract its zero surface. The modified field is not necessarily exact signed distance.

title: Discretizing Geometry I — contours
note: Make one true section curve, then repeat it with a controlled start height, count and interval.

title: Discretizing Geometry II — physical parts
note: Fill and thicken the profiles, compare the stack with separate parts, then lay them out in a grid.

title: Final Project — fabrication and assembly
note: Millimeter examples with STL snapshots and a labeled SVG cutting layout. Test actual stock, joints, fit and kerf before production.
